title: Function-space pCN and invariant posterior kernels

items.title: Borel laws on a separable Hilbert space are determined by basis coordinates
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $H$ be a real Hilbert space with a
finite or countable complete orthonormal basis $(e_j)_{j\in J}$. For each finite
$F\subseteq J$, define the coordinate map
$\pi_F:H\to\mathbb R^F$ by
$\pi_F(x)=(\langle x,e_j\rangle)_{j\in F}$. If $\nu$ and $\nu'$ are Borel
probability measures on $H$ and
$\nu(\pi_F^{-1}(B))=\nu'(\pi_F^{-1}(B))$ for every finite $F\subseteq J$ and
every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^F$, then $\nu=\nu'$.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used through the supplied Parseval theorem and to show that the rational span of the finite or countable basis is countable; the remaining Borel-generation and finite-measure uniqueness arguments use no choice.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis, §2.1, Theorems 2.3–2.4
references.locator: §2.1, Theorems 2.3–2.4, printed pp. 50–51: countable orthonormal bases and Parseval's identity.

items.title: Prior-preserving Crank–Nicolson sampler
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, let
$\mu_0$ be a centered Borel Gaussian probability measure on $H$, let
$D\subseteq H$ be Borel with $\mu_0(D)=1$, and let
$\Phi_D:D\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be Borel. Assume the evidence
$$
Z:=\int_D e^{-\Phi_D(u)}\,\mu_0(du)
$$
satisfies $0<Z<\infty$. Extend the potential to all of $H$ by setting
$\bar\Phi(u)=\Phi_D(u)$ for $u\in D$ and $\bar\Phi(u)=+\infty$ for
$u\notin D$, and define the target probability
$\mu(du)=Z^{-1}e^{-\bar\Phi(u)}\mu_0(du)$. For a scale $\beta\in[0,1]$,
write $\rho=\sqrt{1-\beta^2}$. At state $u\in H$, draw $\xi\sim\mu_0$
independently and propose $v=\rho u+\beta\xi$. Set the acceptance probability
to $0$ if either $\bar\Phi(u)$ or $\bar\Phi(v)$ is $+\infty$, and otherwise set
$$
\alpha(u,v)=\min\{1,\exp(\bar\Phi(u)-\bar\Phi(v))\}.
$$
Draw an independent uniform random variable on $[0,1]$ and move to $v$ if it
is at most $\alpha(u,v)$; otherwise remain at $u$. The resulting one-step
transition rule is the prior-preserving Crank–Nicolson, or pCN, rule
$P_\beta$. States with infinite potential are absorbing under this total
definition; they have $\mu$-measure zero.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed by the library's centered Borel Gaussian interface. The proposal and acceptance instructions add no further choice use.

references.title: S. L. Cotter, G. O. Roberts, A. M. Stuart, and D. White, MCMC Methods for Functions: Modifying Old Algorithms to Make Them Faster, Statistical Science 28(3) (2013)
Yury Korolev and Jonas Latz, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, Michaelmas Term 2020 (University of Cambridge, 18 May 2021)
M. Hairer, A. M. Stuart, and S. J. Vollmer, Spectral gaps for a Metropolis–Hastings algorithm in infinite dimensions, Annals of Applied Probability 24(6) (2014)
references.locator: §2.1, Algorithm 1 and its Gaussian-reference target convention.

items.title: The pCN accept-reject procedure defines a probability kernel
items.statement:
Under the inputs and instructions of the prior-preserving Crank–Nicolson
algorithm, for every $\beta\in[0,1]$ its proposal rule is a Borel probability
kernel and its accept-reject transition $P_\beta$ is a Borel probability
kernel on $H$.
items.axiom_use: No choice is used to prove kernel measurability or the pointwise probability property once the algorithm inputs are supplied.

references.title: S. L. Cotter, G. O. Roberts, A. M. Stuart, and D. White, MCMC Methods for Functions: Modifying Old Algorithms to Make Them Faster, Statistical Science 28(3) (2013)
Yury Korolev and Jonas Latz, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, Michaelmas Term 2020 (University of Cambridge, 18 May 2021)

items.title: The pCN Gaussian reference pair law is symmetric
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space and let
$\mu_0$ be a centered Borel Gaussian probability measure on $H$. Let $U$ and
$\xi$ be independent random elements with law $\mu_0$. For
$\beta\in[0,1]$, set $\rho=\sqrt{1-\beta^2}$ and
$V=\rho U+\beta\xi$. The joint Borel law of $(U,V)$ on $H\times H$ is
unchanged by the coordinate swap $(u,v)\mapsto(v,u)$.
items.axiom_use: AC is used through the Borel Gaussian and multivariate normal interfaces and implies the Countable Choice needed by the coordinate-law supplier. No stronger choice principle is used.

references.title: S. L. Cotter, G. O. Roberts, A. M. Stuart, and D. White, MCMC Methods for Functions: Modifying Old Algorithms to Make Them Faster, Statistical Science 28(3) (2013)
references.locator: §6.1, Theorem 6.2 and proof that the prior flow is symmetric for the Crank–Nicolson choice.

references.title: Yury Korolev and Jonas Latz, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, Michaelmas Term 2020 (University of Cambridge, 18 May 2021)
references.locator: Chapter 8, §8.2, Example 8.2.7 and pCN reference-preserving proposal.

items.title: pCN stationary mean acceptance tends to one at small scale
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a separable real Hilbert space and let
$\mu_0$ be a centered Borel Gaussian probability measure on $H$. Let
$\Phi:H\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued and Borel measurable. Suppose that
there are constants $p,K>0$ such that
$$0\le\Phi(u)\le K(1+\|u\|^p)\qquad(u\in H),$$
and for every $R>0$ there is a finite $L_R$ such that
$$|\Phi(u)-\Phi(v)|\le L_R\|u-v\|\quad\text{whenever }\max\{\|u\|,\|v\|\}<R.$$
Set $Z=\int_H e^{-\Phi(u)}\,\mu_0(du)$ and
$\mu(du)=Z^{-1}e^{-\Phi(u)}\mu_0(du)$. For $\beta\in[0,1]$, let
$U\sim\mu$ and $\xi\sim\mu_0$ be independent, put
$V_\beta=\sqrt{1-\beta^2}U+\beta\xi$, and define
$$\alpha_\beta=\min\{1,\exp(\Phi(U)-\Phi(V_\beta))\}.$$
Then $0<Z<\infty$, $\mu$ is a probability measure, and the stationary mean
acceptance satisfies
$$\lim_{\beta\downarrow0}\mathbb E[\alpha_\beta]=1.$$
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the centered Borel Gaussian and pCN interfaces. The posterior-propriety supplier and the limit argument add no further choice use.

references.title: S. L. Cotter, G. O. Roberts, A. M. Stuart, and D. White, MCMC Methods for Functions: Modifying Old Algorithms to Make Them Faster, Statistical Science 28(3) (2013)
references.locator: §6.2, Assumptions 6.1(1)–(2) and Theorem 6.4; the small-scale acceptance limit is proved locally here.

items.title: The pCN accept-reject kernel preserves the posterior
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the inputs of the prior-preserving
Crank–Nicolson algorithm: a separable real Hilbert space $H$, centered Borel
Gaussian reference probability $\mu_0$, full-mass Borel domain $D$, Borel
potential $\Phi_D:D\to(-\infty,+\infty]$, positive finite evidence $Z$, and
scale $\beta\in[0,1]$. Let $\mu$ be the normalized target on $H$ obtained by
extending $\Phi_D$ by $+\infty$ off $D$, and let $P_\beta$ be the algorithm's
accept-reject transition. Then $P_\beta$ is reversible with respect to $\mu$:
its joint flow
$$\Lambda_\beta(C):=\int_H P_\beta(u,C_u)\,\mu(du),\qquad C_u:=\{v\in H:(u,v)\in C\},$$
is unchanged by $(u,v)\mapsto(v,u)$ for every Borel
$C\subseteq H\times H$. Consequently, $\mu$ is invariant:
$$\int_H P_\beta(u,A)\,\mu(du)=\mu(A)\qquad(A\in\mathcal B(H)).$$
This conclusion gives invariance only; it does not assert uniqueness,
convergence, mixing, an effective-sample-size bound, mesh-independent cost,
or correctness of an approximate forward solver.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the pCN Gaussian-reference algorithm. The symmetric-flow argument uses no further choice principle.

references.title: S. L. Cotter, G. O. Roberts, A. M. Stuart, and D. White, MCMC Methods for Functions: Modifying Old Algorithms to Make Them Faster, Statistical Science 28(3) (2013)
references.locator: §4.2, equation (4.7); §6.1, Theorem 6.2; prior-preserving pCN detailed-balance correction.

references.locator: Chapter 8, §8.2, Definition 8.2.3 and Proposition 8.2.4, complete Metropolis–Hastings detailed-balance proof.

title: Function-space pCN and invariant posterior kernels — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Infinite-dimensional Gaussian random-walk reverse flow is singular
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix $\beta\in(0,1]$. Let
$H=\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ with its complete coordinate basis positively indexed as $(e_j)_{j\ge1}$, where $e_j$ has its nonzero coordinate at $j-1$. Write $u_j=\langle u,e_j\rangle$ for coefficients in this basis throughout. Take
mutually independent standard normal variables $(X_j,Y_j)_{j\ge1}$ and set
$$U=\sum_{j\ge1}2^{-j/2}X_je_j,\qquad \xi=\sum_{j\ge1}2^{-j/2}Y_je_j.$$
These series converge almost surely in $H$ and define independent centered
Borel Gaussian random elements with the same law $\mu_0$. Define the Gaussian
random-walk proposal $V=U+\beta\xi$, its probability kernel
$$Q_\beta(u,B)=\mu_0(\{z\in H:u+\beta z\in B\}),$$
its forward flow $\eta(du,dv)=\mu_0(du)Q_\beta(u,dv)$, and its transpose
$\eta^\top(C)=\eta(\{(u,v):(v,u)\in C\})$. Then $\eta$ and $\eta^\top$ are
mutually singular: a Borel set $A_\beta\subseteq H\times H$ satisfies
$$\eta(A_\beta)=1,\qquad \eta^\top(A_\beta)=0.$$
For the same reference law and scale, the pCN proposal flow is symmetric.
items.axiom_use: AC supplies dependent and countable choice for the iid Gaussian sequence and the Gaussian-series law; the strong-law and separating-event arguments add no choice use.

references.title: S. L. Cotter, G. O. Roberts, A. M. Stuart, and D. White, MCMC Methods for Functions: Modifying Old Algorithms to Make Them Faster, Statistical Science 28(3) (2013)
references.locator: §4.2, equation (4.3), and §6.1, Theorem 6.3; a coordinate strong-law separator is proved locally here.

references.title: Yury Korolev and Jonas Latz, Inverse Problems: Lecture Notes, Michaelmas Term 2020 (University of Cambridge, 18 May 2021)
references.locator: Chapter 8, §8.2, Examples 8.2.6–8.2.7, random-walk and pCN proposals.

items.title: A Gaussian pCN kernel leaves a normal posterior invariant
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H=\mathbb R$, give the unknown parameter $u$ the prior law
$\mu_0=N(0,1)$, and observe one datum $Y=0$ from the model
$Y\mid u\sim N(u,1)$. The Gaussian conjugate update gives posterior
$\mu=N(0,1/2)$. Use the potential $\Phi(u)=u^2/2$ in the pCN algorithm. For
$\beta\in[0,1]$, write $\rho=\sqrt{1-\beta^2}$, propose
$v=\rho u+\beta\xi$ with $\xi\sim N(0,1)$ independent of the current
state, and accept with probability
$$\alpha(u,v)=\min\{1,\exp((u^2-v^2)/2)\}.$$
The resulting pCN probability kernel leaves $N(0,1/2)$ invariant for every
$\beta\in[0,1]$.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the normal-law and pCN interfaces; no additional choice is used in the calculation.
